questionnaire_prompt: Select up to five issues that matter most to you, then choose your House or Senate district to compare candidate priorities.

profiles.summary: My campaign is focused on five key priorities.

priorities.title: Making Rhode Island More Affordable
priorities.summary: Working to lower the cost of living by addressing rising utility costs, expanding consumer protections, supporting affordable housing, and ensuring working families can keep more of what they earn.

priorities.title: Expanding Access to Healthcare
priorities.summary: Strengthening our healthcare workforce by improving provider retention, supporting primary care, increasing access to preventive and mental healthcare, and ensuring every Rhode Islander can access quality, affordable care.

priorities.title: Government Accountability and Transparency
priorities.summary: Promoting ethical, transparent government that is responsive to residents, protects taxpayer dollars, and restores public trust through greater accountability.

priorities.title: Building a Stronger Economy for Working Families
priorities.summary: Supporting small businesses, investing in workforce development, creating good-paying jobs, and ensuring economic growth benefits working families, not just large corporations.

priorities.title: Investing in Safe, Healthy, and Sustainable Communities
priorities.summary: Improving infrastructure, supporting public education, expanding clean energy that reduces costs for consumers, protecting our environment, and creating neighborhoods where families can thrive.

profiles.summary: Michael J. Riley, known as Lou, is a third-generation Scituate resident, solo-practice real estate attorney, husband, and father of four running in House District 41.

priorities.title: Repeal the Assault Weapons Ban
priorities.summary: The assault weapons ban took effect on July 1 and, in his view, will not stop crime while turning law-abiding residents into criminals. He says he will vote to repeal it.

priorities.title: Local Control of Zoning and Land Use
priorities.summary: If something is getting built in Scituate, he believes Scituate should decide. He says the state keeps overriding local planning and zoning boards and that he will fight to restore local control.

priorities.title: Taxes and Cost of Living
priorities.summary: He points to the conveyance-tax increase, Rhode Island's non-portable estate tax starting below $2 million, the non-owner-occupied surcharge, and business surtaxes as reasons it is getting more expensive both to live in Rhode Island and to pass assets on to family.

priorities.title: Schools and Parental Voice
priorities.summary: He wants more money to reach classrooms, more secure school buildings, and a stronger voice for parents. As a father of four, he says this is a personal priority.

priorities.title: Keeping Doctors in Rhode Island
priorities.summary: He argues that long waits for primary-care appointments, residents driving to Massachusetts, and doctors closing practices or leaving the state all show a healthcare access problem that the legislature should address.
